record.field: Absent or Failed Defences
AFD
Identify physical, procedural, or administrative barriers that were absent, inadequate, or failed to prevent the incident from occurring.
Individual / Team Actions
ITA
Identify actions (or inactions) by individuals or teams that directly contributed to the incident. These are the things people did or failed to do.
Task / Environmental Conditions
TEC
Identify conditions related to the task, equipment, or work environment that influenced the individual or team actions contributing to the incident.
Organisational Factors
OF
Identify systemic, management system, or organisational influences that created or allowed the conditions and actions that led to the incident.
Physical barriers / guards absent or failed
Physical guards, barriers, interlocks or containment systems were not in place or did not function as intended.
Warning or alarm systems absent or failed
Warning devices, alarms, signals, or indicator systems were absent, not functioning, or not perceived by those involved.
Administrative / procedural controls absent or failed
Policies, procedures, permits, or administrative safeguards were not in place, were inadequate, or were not applied.
Training / competency assurance absent or failed
Training, competency assessment, or authorisation processes were not in place or did not ensure the required level of competency.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) absent or failed
Required PPE was not available, not worn, inadequate for the hazard, or failed to provide the expected protection.
Emergency response / recovery absent or failed
Emergency response plans, resources, or capabilities were insufficient to prevent or limit the severity of the incident.
Procedure / instruction not followed
An established procedure, work instruction, or safe work method statement existed but was not followed by the individual or team.
Incorrect procedure applied
The wrong procedure or method was applied to the task, either through error or misidentification of the applicable document.
No procedure / instruction available
No procedure, work instruction, or guidance existed for the task being undertaken at the time of the incident.
Communication failure between individuals
Inadequate, incorrect, or absent communication between individuals or teams contributed to the incident.
Fatigue / fitness for work
Fatigue, illness, or impairment affected the individual's ability to perform the task safely.
Complacency / normalisation of deviance
Over-familiarity with the task led to risk-taking or shortcuts that had become accepted practice despite not being compliant with safe work requirements.
Poor situational awareness
The individual or team did not adequately perceive, comprehend, or anticipate the hazard or changing conditions.
Error in decision making
An incorrect decision was made in relation to the task, hazard, or risk, leading to or contributing to the incident.
Incorrect tool / equipment selected or used
The wrong tool, equipment, or method was selected or used for the task.
Time pressure / excessive workload
Pressure to complete the task quickly or an excessive workload influenced the actions taken.
Environmental conditions (heat, cold, noise, lighting, etc.)
Physical environmental factors such as extreme temperature, poor lighting, excessive noise, or adverse weather contributed to the incident.
Housekeeping / workplace layout
Poor housekeeping, congestion, or inadequate workplace layout contributed to the incident.
Equipment / plant condition
The condition of equipment, plant, or tools (e.g. wear, damage, inadequate maintenance) contributed to the incident.
Distractions / interruptions
Distractions or interruptions during the task affected the individual's ability to perform it safely.
Ergonomics / posture / physical demands
Ergonomic factors, awkward posture, repetitive movements, or physical demands of the task contributed to the incident.
Unfamiliar task or non-routine situation
The task was unfamiliar, infrequent, or the situation was unusual, reducing the individual's ability to manage the associated risks.
Inadequate supervision of task
The level of supervision provided was insufficient given the nature and risk of the task.
Risk management / hazard identification process
The organisation's risk assessment, hazard identification, or risk control processes were absent, inadequate, or not applied.
Management systems / procedures inadequate
The organisation's management system, policies, or documented procedures were inadequate or not effectively implemented.
Leadership and safety culture
Leadership behaviours, organisational culture, or safety climate influenced the conditions or actions that led to the incident.
Contractor / subcontractor management
Inadequate management, selection, induction, or oversight of contractors or subcontractors contributed to the incident.
Change management process
Changes to plant, equipment, procedures, personnel, or work scope were not adequately assessed or communicated through a management of change process.
Resource allocation / planning
Inadequate allocation of resources (people, time, equipment, budget) to safely complete the work contributed to the incident.
Organisational communication systems
Systemic failures in how safety-critical information is communicated across the organisation contributed to the incident.
Training and competency management systems
The organisation's systems for identifying training needs, delivering training, and assessing competency were inadequate.
Fatigue risk management
Rosters, shift arrangements, or fatigue management systems did not adequately manage the risk of worker fatigue.
Procurement / maintenance management systems
Systems for procuring fit-for-purpose equipment or maintaining it in a safe condition were inadequate.
